summary: X-Dev-Seed-Mock header opt-in VERIFIED. Both /api/chat/init-mock and /api/chat/conversations correctly honor request.headers.get('x-dev-seed-mock','')=='1' (FastAPI lowercase normalization works fine when sending 'X-Dev-Seed-Mock: 1'). New iter24 suite: 7/7 PASS — 2a init-mock without header is skipped, 2b with header seeds 3 mock convos, 2c re-GET without header preserves the 3 seeded and does NOT add Anjali Iyer / Priya Bhatia, 2d brand-new user with no header gets [], 2e brand-new user with header gets >=2 (Anjali Iyer + Priya Bhatia seeded). Regression #5 also PASS — fresh user no header => []. test_audit_iter20.py: ALL 20/20 PASS (previous 4 cascading failures in TestMatchFlowPersistence::test_b/test_c/test_f/test_g are RESOLVED — header pattern in the fixture works end-to-end through /chat/accept, /chat/decline, /chat/delete, meeting-report). test_supabase_audit.py: 13/13 PASS. test_launch_prep_iter22.py: 7/8 PASS — the one failure (test_matchmaking_mixed_pool) is PRE-EXISTING organic pool-size drift (real-user pool grew to 150+, bots get truncated below top-15 cut — same root cause as iter23's flaky test_real_user_appears_in_bobs_feed) and is UNRELATED to the header opt-in change. context_for_next_testing_agent: The 4 cascading failures from iter22/iter23 in test_audit_iter20.py::TestMatchFlowPersistence are FIXED via the X-Dev-Seed-Mock header (no env-var flipping needed). Header is lowercased by FastAPI/Starlette so the backend reads it as 'x-dev-seed-mock'. Both /chat/init-mock and /chat/conversations honor it; /user/match-history is intentionally env-var-only. Pre-existing flake test_launch_prep_iter22.py::test_matchmaking_mixed_pool is the only remaining failure and is unrelated — pool-rank drift, same family as iter23's test_real_user_appears_in_bobs_feed. Production behavior (no header, no env var) is verified clean: fresh user => [] conversations, no Anjali/Priya pollution.
rca_of_issue: Root cause of the iter22/23 test cascade: /chat/init-mock had its DEV_SEED_MOCK_CHATS=1 env gate added in iter22, and /chat/conversations got its DEV_SEED_MOCK_UNMATCHED=1 gate added in iter23. Together these correctly removed mock pollution from production users but left the audit tests dependent on side-effect seeding with no way to opt-in per-call. Fix in iter24 adds an OR-clause header check (`request.headers.get('x-dev-seed-mock','')=='1'`) at both endpoints — gives the audit suite a per-request opt-in without mutating process env. Verified by running test_audit_iter20.py: all 20/20 pass; the previously-broken test_b_init_mock_then_accept_NEW_HOOK + downstream test_c_decline / test_f_delete / test_g_meeting_report are now GREEN.
